usual_baseline: Fasting is almost always too long: clear fluids mean 10.5 hours, solids 15.8 hours; 62% 'nil by mouth from midnight' [1641]. Only 39% got their usual medicines while fasting [1630]. Unnecessary tests are routine: 91% of ASA 1–2 abscess patients had bloods [2661]; 81% of coagulation screens inappropriate [2255].
fix_that_works: Posters and dissemination: abscess bloods 91% to 27%, £2,151 to £406 [2661]. Coagulation appropriate 19% to 56% [2255]. Decision aid cut ASA 2 FBCs by 75.0% [2835]. Patient leaflets: clear fluid fasting median 10 to 3 hours [2356]. Drug trolley posters: correct medicines 39% to 61% [1630]. Liquid fasting 10% to 60% [2065].
fix_that_fails: SipTilSend lapsed: fluid fasting rose from 3 h 45 min to 11.2 hours despite reinforcement [1191]. Solid fasting did not improve: 5% to 0% [2065], median 12.5 to 11 hours [2356].
consultant_advice: Fasting audits are common and relapse fast, so measure sustainability months later rather than another baseline. Unnecessary bloods before minor surgery are a quick, cheap win with cost figures. Omitted critical medicines while nil by mouth are less audited and more important.
